Abstract
To address the problem of security analysis lag caused by the delay in dynamic 
topology updates in short video networks, this paper constructs a real-time digital 
twin framework based on edge computing lightweight proxies and achieves 
low-delay state response by accelerating the state synchronizer through field-
programmable gate array (FPGA). For cross-modal attack detection blind spots, a 
joint analysis model is constructed by combining network topology and content 
features to improve the ability to identify complex threats and predict evolution 
trends. A lightweight proxy module is deployed on the content delivery network 
(CDN) node. Docker containerization technology is used to collect device states, user 
behavior, and traffic feature data in real time to build a local topology subgraph. 
A parallel state processor based on pipeline architecture. Incremental updates of 
the topological relationship matrix (500 × 500) are implemented, and the clock 
cycle is optimized through hardware description language. By integrating graph 
attention network (GAT) and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers 
(BERT) text encoders, a three-dimensional feature space of “node-edge-content” is 
established to detect topological anomalies and content violation coupled attacks 
of disguised accounts. A spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (STGCN) is 
constructed to extract topological evolution patterns in a fixed time window and 
predict the propagation paths of high-risk nodes. Experimental results show that 
the synchronization delay of FPGA tends to 0.5ms in the topology synchronization 
change time of 100ms, which has a high response speed; in the four types of cross-
modal coordinated attack scenarios, the average identification precision and recall of 
the joint analysis model in this paper are 91.9%±0.9% and 88.7%±1.4%, respectively, 
and its cross-modal attack identification performance is strong; in the prediction 
of node connection probability, the root mean squared error (RMSE) of STGCN 
is 6.84 ± 0.31 at a time offset of 2.5 s, which verifies the model’s ability to predict 
evolution trends; the total end-to-end delay is 7.5ms. In the 72-hour continuous 
stress test, the central processing unit (CPU) usage rate is 8.3%→9.1%; the memory 
leak rate is < 0.01%/h; the false positive rate for abnormal events is 0.7%→1.2%; the 
prediction error accumulation rate is 0.05%/h, verifying the long-term prediction 
stability. The data results demonstrate the effectiveness of this paper’s research on 
secure propagation analysis of short videos and evolution trend prediction.

1  Introduction
 Short video networks’ dynamic characteristics have given rise to new security threats, 
such as cross-modal coordinated attacks and instantaneous propagation path variations 
[1, 2]. Digital twin technology has become a key enabler for real-time security analy­
sis due to its high-fidelity mapping capabilities [3, 4]. The combination of FPGA’s hard­
ware reconfigurability and graph neural network’s spatio-temporal modeling capabilities 
provides a new paradigm for building a fast-response dynamic protection system [5, 6]. 
The coordinated deployment of edge computing and lightweight proxies [7, 8] further 
improves the granularity and real-time performance of network state perception.
Current research on secure propagation networks for short videos faces several key 
challenges. In terms of topological dynamics, the network structure exhibits nonlinear 
evolution features, and the node connection pattern changes suddenly on a millisecond 
time scale. The state synchronization mechanism of the existing digital twin framework 
makes it difficult to match this rate of change [9, 10]. Hardware acceleration solutions 
are limited by the inherent delay of the computing architecture and find it difficult to 
strike a balance between scalability and real-time performance [11, 12]. Cross-modal 
threat detection suffers from the problem of fragmented analysis dimensions. The cor­
relation between topological features and content semantics is not fully modeled, and 
attack behaviors are hidden from a single detection perspective [13, 14]. For example, 
malicious accounts may conceal the spread of abnormal content through normal inter­
active behaviors. However, existing methods lack the ability to jointly infer the “struc­
ture-semantics” coupling relationship [15, 16]. The time series prediction model is not 
adaptable enough. The short video propagation path is driven by hot topics, which are 
sudden and time-varying. Static graph neural networks cannot capture the high-order 
patterns of short-term topological evolution [17, 18]. The existing time series modeling 
methods have limited prediction precision in fine-grained time windows and are difficult 
to support real-time risk intervention decisions. In addition, distributed data collection 
faces a balance between privacy and efficiency. The local topology subgraphs generated 
by edge nodes need to be efficiently aggregated while protecting user information. Exist­
ing privacy protection mechanisms may undermine the integrity of the network struc­
ture and affect the credibility of global security analysis [19, 20]. These challenges jointly 
restrict the effectiveness of security protection in dynamic network environments, and 
there is an urgent need to build a collaborative analysis framework that considers real-
time response, multimodal fusion, and privacy protection.
This paper aims to build a new short video security protection paradigm, break 
through the mindset of static analysis framework, and realize the “predictive sniping” 
of network threats. Unlike the passive defense mode, this study creatively transforms 
digital twin technology into a “tactical sandbox” in the dynamic offensive and defensive 
battlefield. Its core innovation is reflected in multiple dimensions. It studies and designs 
a new paradigm of hardware-aware topological computing. Through the collaborative 
design of FPGA reconfigurable computing architecture and pipelined state processor, it 
realizes the quantized synchronous update of network topology, enabling digital twins to

2  Related work
Existing research on short video network security issues mainly focuses on the two 
dimensions of topological feature extraction and time series modeling. In terms of 
topology synchronization, some use graphics processing unit (GPU) parallel comput­
ing to accelerate adjacency matrix updates, but the maximum supported node size is 
limited due to video memory limitations [21, 22]. Some researchers have developed 
application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) chips to achieve topology state synchro­
nization [23, 24]. Satyanarayanan M believed that Silent Witness is a new type of edge 
computing abstraction that emphasizes privacy control. It alleviates the contradiction 
between artificial intelligence (AI) and privacy by limiting the decryption and process­
ing of data. To improve its search efficiency in monitoring scenarios, the use of decod­
ing-supported storage and ASIC acceleration significantly improves system throughput, 
with performance improved by 3.5 times [25]. Although these methods can reduce delay 
to a certain extent, they lack the flexibility of dynamic reconstruction. In attack detec­
tion, some studies based on graph convolutional networks (GCN) degree centrality anal­
ysis can identify highly abnormal nodes but cannot detect content semantic violations 
[26, 27]. In terms of time series prediction, the temporal graph convolutional network 
(TGCN) model captures the topological evolution law through a time sliding window, 
but the granular sampling interval leads to high prediction errors of hotspot propaga­
tion paths [28, 29]. Liu X proposed a TGCN model that integrates the attention mecha­
nism to improve the accuracy of information propagation prediction. By integrating user 
influence relationships, behavioral dynamics, and time factors, the model significantly 
outperforms existing models on multiple datasets and has practical application value in 
rumor monitoring and malicious account identification [30]. Existing methods generally 
have some limitations. Hardware acceleration solutions are difficult to balance between 
real-time performance and scalability. Single-modal detection models cannot cope with 
complex attacks. The granularity of time series modeling does not match the dynamic 
propagation rate.

Digital twin technology provides a new approach to solving the above problems. 
Recent studies have shown that the digital twin framework based on edge computing 
can reduce the delay of topology updates, but its software-defined synchronizer is still 
limited by the CPU instruction cycle [31, 32]. In terms of cross-modal analysis, some 
scholars have integrated GAT with the visual Transformer model to achieve a high mul­

acteristics [33, 34]. It is worth noting that the dynamic reconfiguration feature of FPGA 
provides a new path for hardware acceleration, which can realize low-delay matrix oper­
ations. Jia C proposed a hardware-oriented neural image compression system, which 
achieved efficient operation on the FPGA platform through a block-based adaptive 
method and energy-saving neural network deployment strategy. The system combines 
the network reconfigurable architecture with quantization-aware training technology to 
effectively improve the real-time processing capability and energy efficiency of 4 K ultra-
high-definition neural video coding on edge devices [35]. However, this method has not 
yet been applied to network topology update scenarios. Digital twin technology has been 
widely used in different fields. Zhou X proposed a multi-model fusion small target detec­
tion model. By fusing shallow and deep features, it can achieve dynamic synchronization 
and high-precision detection of equipment, products, and operators in the intelligent 
manufacturing digital twin system, and verify its effectiveness in various scenarios [36]. 
Lv Z built a traffic accident prediction and prevention system based on digital twin and 
artificial intelligence. By using a dual-scale LSTM prediction model and an improved 
particle filter target tracking algorithm, the system improves prediction accuracy and 
processing efficiency. Compared with traditional models, it has obvious advantages in 
accuracy, robustness, and speed [37]. Zhang K proposed a social-aware vehicle edge 
caching mechanism. Combining digital twin and deep learning, it builds a social rela­
tionship model and an on-board cache cloud in the virtual space, realizes multi-vehicle 
collaborative cache resource allocation, and thus significantly improves content deliv­
ery efficiency [38]. This paper innovatively constructs a digital twin system that com­
bines software and hardware: at the hardware level, an FPGA-based state synchronizer 
is designed to break through the bottleneck of the von Neumann architecture through a 
parallel pipeline architecture; at the algorithm level, a three-dimensional feature space 
modeling method is designed to perform a tensor fusion of node connection patterns 
(GAT extraction), content semantic features (BERT encoding), and temporal evolution 
laws (STGCN capture); at the architecture level, a containerized proxy is used to imple­
ment the “collection-processing-modeling” closed loop, and the data transmission load 
is reduced by splicing local topology subgraphs. Compared with traditional solutions, 
this framework achieves breakthroughs in three dimensions: real-time topology syn­
chronization, comprehensive attack detection, and accuracy of evolution prediction.

dimensional network traffic data in real time and achieve millisecond-level transmission 
through encrypted data pipelines. A hardware-algorithm collaborative computing center

3.1  Edge computing lightweight proxy deployment
Lightweight proxy modules are deployed on CDN nodes. Docker containerization tech­
nology is used to collect device states, user behavior, and traffic feature data in real time. 
Local topology subgraphs are constructed.

node runs an independent Docker container, and the container image integrates the data

(source IP, destination IP, source port, destination port, and transport protocol), packet 
size, timestamp, and other metadata, and parses hypertext transfer protocol (HTTP)/
hypertext transfer protocol secure (HTTPS) headers to extract user request features 
(User-Agent, Referer, Content-Type, and other fields). User behavior data is intercepted

4.1  Entropy evolution and spatio-temporal distribution of container resources under

The entropy evolution data source is used to build a network traffic mirror based on lib­
pcap capture, including full data packet capture of CDN nodes for 24 consecutive hours. 
The raw data is classified and processed by the protocol parsing engine: HTTP traffic 
extracts the Host header field and path; HTTPS traffic identifies the field and certificate 
fingerprint; UDP traffic associates the protocol flow ID. In the feature engineering stage, 
the target port distribution is counted in a 10-second sliding window with a window 
step of 5 s and an overlap rate of 50% to balance timeliness and computing overhead. 
The entropy calculation follows the definition of flow characteristics. The statistics in 
the window are defined as discrete random variables with a value space of 1,024 stan­
dard port numbers (0–1,023). The probability density is obtained by normalizing the 
port occurrence frequency. Protocol differentiation is achieved through L4 layer packet 
header parsing, HTTP/HTTPS traffic is separated based on ports, and UDP traffic filters 
common service ports such as ports 53 and 123. During the anomaly injection stage, 
simulated attack traffic is inserted into the UDP data stream: a 100:1 domain name 
system (DNS) response request ratio is generated during the 12:00–12:15 period, with 
forged source IP accounting for 35%, generating a traffic distribution that conforms to 
the characteristics of a reflection attack. The 3σ criterion is used for data cleaning to 
remove outliers, and finally, a synthetic dataset that conforms to the statistical charac­
teristics of the real network is generated.

5  Conclusion
This study builds a dynamic protection system for secure propagation networks for 
short videos, breaking through the limitations of traditional static analysis frameworks. 
It innovatively integrates edge computing, FPGA acceleration, and multimodal graph 
neural network technology to achieve quantized synchronization between physical net­
works and digital twins, providing a new paradigm for security protection in complex 
network environments.
On the theoretical level, a hardware-algorithm collaborative topological comput­
ing architecture is adopted, and nanosecond-level incremental updates of the 500 × 500 
adjacency matrix are achieved through an FPGA pipelined state processor, overcoming 
the key difficulty of real-time mapping of dynamic network topologies. The designed 
“node-edge-content” three-dimensional feature space, combined with graph attention 
mechanism and semantic coding technology, realizes quantum entanglement correla­
tion analysis of topological anomalies and content violations, and improves the detection 
sensitivity of cross-modal coordinated attacks. The spatio-temporal graph convolutional 
network precisely captures the chaotic characteristics of network evolution through 
layered spatio-temporal feature extraction and dynamic gating mechanism, enabling 
security protection to leap from post-tracing to a new dimension of pre-prediction. At 
the engineering practice level, the containerized deployment solution of the lightweight 
proxy module balances data collection efficiency and privacy protection requirements. 
Local topology subgraph splicing technology ensures the credibility of global security 
analysis. Experimental verification shows that the system surpasses existing solutions in 
millisecond-level response, multimodal threat identification, and propagation path pre­
diction, laying the foundation for building an autonomously evolving intelligent defense 
system. However, there may be some limitations when expanding this framework to 
larger network topologies or more complex content types. The hardware resource limi­
tations of FPGA may restrict the scale expansion of the adjacency matrix, resulting in 
challenges in real-time synchronization of ultra-large-scale networks. The computa­
tional complexity of multimodal feature fusion increases exponentially with the increase 
in content type, which may affect the system response speed. In addition, the adaptabil­
ity issues of heterogeneous hardware environments during cross-platform deployment 
may weaken the versatility of the framework. In the future, it is necessary to explore 
distributed digital twin architectures and lightweight multimodal encoders to break 
through the above bottlenecks. At the same time, explore the distributed twin collabora­
tive optimization under the federated learning framework to further expand the model’s 
generalization capabilities against new adversarial attacks.

Abstract: To address the problem of security analysis lag caused by the delay in dynamic topology updates in short video networks, this paper constructs a real-time digital twin framework based on edge computing lightweight proxies and achieves low-delay state response by accelerating the state synchronizer through field- programmable gate array (FPGA). For cross-modal attack detection blind spots, a joint analysis model is constructed by combining network topology and content features to improve the ability to identify complex threats and predict evolution trends. A lightweight proxy module is deployed on the content delivery network (CDN) node. Docker containerization technology is used to collect device states, user behavior, and traffic feature data in real time to build a local topology subgraph. A parallel state processor based on pipeline architecture. Incremental updates of the topological relationship matrix (500 × 500) are implemented, and the clock cycle is optimized through hardware description language. By integrating graph attention network (GAT) and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) text encoders, a three-dimensional feature space of “node-edge-content” is established to detect topological anomalies and content violation coupled attacks of disguised accounts. A spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (STGCN) is constructed to extract topological evolution patterns in a fixed time window and predict the propagation paths of high-risk nodes. Experimental results show that the synchronization delay of FPGA tends to 0.5ms in the topology synchronization change time of 100ms, which has a high response speed; in the four types of cross- modal coordinated attack scenarios, the average identification precision and recall of the joint analysis model in this paper are 91.9%±0.9% and 88.7%±1.4%, respectively, and its cross-modal attack identification performance is strong; in the prediction of node connection probability, the root mean squared error (RMSE) of STGCN is 6.84 ± 0.31 at a time offset of 2.5 s, which verifies the model’s ability to predict evolution trends; the total end-to-end delay is 7.5ms. In the 72-hour continuous stress test, the central processing unit (CPU) usage rate is 8.3%→9.1%; the memory leak rate is < 0.01%/h; the false positive rate for abnormal events is 0.7%→1.2%; the prediction error accumulation rate is 0.05%/h, verifying the long-term prediction stability. The data results demonstrate the effectiveness of this paper’s research on secure propagation analysis of short videos and evolution trend prediction.
